title: SE(3) diffusion model with application to protein backbone generation
layout_note: Two panels side by side. Left: one network layer as three horizontal lanes - node embedding h (top, through a grey 'NodeUpdate' container, with h0 entering above it), edge embedding z (middle, through a small 'EdgeUpdate' box) and frames T (bottom, through a 'BackboneUpdate' box) - each entering at the left as a glyph and leaving at the right as its l+1 symbol; the new node embedding drops down into the edge and backbone updates. Right: the EdgeUpdate box opened up as its own panel, with a legend for the concatenate and skip-connection glyphs beneath.
grouping: Colour codes the stream: everything of the node update is orange (container outline, arrows, dotted sub-block outlines), everything of the edge update is cyan; the frame lane and BackboneUpdate stay black. The expanded EdgeUpdate panel repeats the cyan outline of the small EdgeUpdate box on the left, which ties the two panels together.
shapes_depth: Grey-filled rectangles with a coloured outline for the update modules; trainable networks inside are small boxes with dotted coloured outlines (Linear, Transformer, MLP, Invariant Point Attention). Inputs are data glyphs: h as short vertical strips of cells (yellow for h0, green for h_l), z as a small blue grid, T as a red three-pronged frame glyph. Circle-plus for the skip connection, a circle with vertical bars for concatenation. Bold math labels.
proposed_highlight: No 'ours' marking; the two update streams are distinguished by colour (orange node update, cyan edge update), and the edge update is expanded in a detail panel drawn in its own colour.
lesson: Draw the residue frame as a tiny three-axis glyph next to T and give it its own black lane under the coloured node and edge lanes, so the reader sees which stream updates geometry and which updates features.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF (first page: 'Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning'; venue_source: pdf). The paper's Figure 1 (backbone frames and noise-to-backbone frames) was opened but not carded; this card is the module-detail figure. The whole figure is one embedded raster in the PDF (refs crop recorded one image covering the crop), so photo_share is null.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: SE(3) protein backbone diffusion score network layer

insights.structure: Left panel shows one layer as three horizontal lanes (node h through a grey NodeUpdate container, edge z through an EdgeUpdate box, frames T through a BackboneUpdate box); right panel opens EdgeUpdate with a small glyph legend beneath.
insights.data: Each lane's input is a tiny glyph: h0/h_l as green-yellow cell columns, z_l as a blue cell grid, T_l as a red three-armed frame; outputs are the bold symbols h_{l+1}, z_{l+1}, T_{l+1}.
insights.emphasis: Colour codes the stream: all NodeUpdate parts and arrows orange, all EdgeUpdate parts cyan (outline repeated in the zoom panel), frames black.
insights.flow: Left-to-right in each lane; the new node embedding drops down in orange into the edge and backbone updates, and inside the zoom h^m, h^n feed down into concatenations along the z line.
insights.avoid: Orange lines from z and T rise into the IPA box and cross the black lanes, which clutters the lower-left corner.

arrangement.units: three unframed horizontal lanes (node in a grey orange-outlined container, edge, frame) in the left panel; a grey cyan-outlined EdgeUpdate detail panel at right
arrangement.inputs_as: small glyphs (cell columns, grid, frame axes) with bold math labels
arrangement.shared: updated node embedding feeds edge and backbone lanes
